generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table, never NULL; every instance appends exactly table_sizes_per_instance rows per table (musical=7, actor=9) with no jitter; generated PKs must be fresh against the compact DB: offset the PK range above max(original PK) (musical.Musical_ID >= 8, actor.Actor_ID >= 9) and dedup against schema.original_values so rows_skipped stays 0; writer reports rows_added/rows_skipped per table. The offset is computed once per table in build_random_instance (fresh_pk_start(schema, table, column)) and the concrete [lo,hi] is passed to the sampler; spec.RANGES PK entries are relative offsets and the module-level _SCHEMA_REF indirection is removed.
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: Draw from parent primary-key pool with replacement; 5-30% NULL when nullable; plant at least one non-NULL child FK value that matches no parent (unmatched join) and ensure at least one parent row has no children; NULLs are planted last and never overwritten by later passes.
generic_sampling_rules.int_numeric: Uniform integer in [min, max] from statistics; boundary values min-1, min, min+1, max-1, max, max+1 are allowed to be generated even when outside the semantic range (they are the comparison-boundary targets); never NULL for NOT NULL columns.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Draw from a small pool of realistic values; 20-50% duplicate share on DISTINCT-targeted columns; include near-variants (case changes, trailing/leading spaces, truncations) of listed literals at a small probability (~10%).
generic_sampling_rules.text_nullable: 5-30% NULL share planted last; non-NULL values from pool with near-variants; NULL positions are skipped by group-size, duplicate and order-tie passes.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Draw from the explicit enum list; include near-variants of each literal for comparison-boundary coverage at a small probability (~10%).
generic_sampling_rules.order_tie: Ensure at least two rows share the top value of the ORDER column so rank-1 ties occur; for ASC force the minimum value to appear at least twice, for DESC force the maximum; direction per column exception; order-tie pass runs on positions disjoint from group-size and duplicate passes.
generic_sampling_rules.group_size: Ensure groups of size 1, 2, and >=3 exist on the GROUP column; group-size pass runs before order-tie pass and on disjoint positions; NULL positions are excluded from group pools; assert per instance that targets were met on the full 7/9-row batches.

dependencies.note: Declared FK in schema points to actor(Actor_ID) which is self-referential and intentionally ignored; logical FK is actor.Musical_ID -> musical.Musical_ID per atomic operations. The declared self-FK is intentionally unenforced (writer sets pragma foreign_keys = OFF); the logical FK is the operative dependency.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: validity.invalid = 7 with reason 'no_rows_added' (7 of 20 instances added zero generated rows). writer.py appends generated rows to a copy of the compact DB; instance.py builds rows but the writer's per-table insert loop uses `n = len(cols.get(names[0], []))`. When the first column of a table is a logical-FK column that was excluded from `samplers` (actor.Musical_ID is a logical FK, so it is not in `samplers`), `cols` for that table is built only from non-FK columns, but `names[0]` is the first declared column. For `actor`, the first declared column is `Actor_ID` (present), so this is not the direct cause; however the observed 0-row instances indicate the generated dict is empty for at least one table in those units, and the writer silently writes nothing rather than failing. The CLI reports `rows_added: {}` and `rows_skipped: {}` (never populated), so the zero-row outcome is invisible in the summary.

issues.evidence: spec.py NULL_SHARE sets ('actor','Musical_ID')=0.20 and ('musical','Nominee')=0.20, and instance._plant_nulls plants NULLs. But execution feedback shows 'musical.Nominee: generated rows: NULL 0 / 11' and 'actor.Musical_ID: generated rows: NULL 1 / 18'. The Nominee NULL rule is not realized at all. Cause: _plant_nulls runs on `cols` after sample_fresh_primary_keys/drop_unique_duplicates, but for musical the Nominee column is present; the 0/11 indicates the planted NULLs were overwritten or the column was regenerated. In build_random_instance, _plant_nulls is called, then _force_group_sizes/_force_duplicates/_force_order_tie run afterward on Nominee (it is in GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS, DUP_COLUMNS, ORDER_TIES), and _force_duplicates/_force_group_sizes draw from `pool = [v for v in vals if v is not None]` and reassign positions including previously-NULL slots, erasing planted NULLs.

issues.evidence: spec.RANGES sets ('actor','age')=(1,60) and BOUNDARY_VALUES ('actor','age')=[-1,0,1], but _init_sampler filters boundary values to `lo <= b <= hi`, so -1 and 0 are dropped and only 1 survives. The comparison_boundary target for actor.age explicitly lists values [-1,0,1] and the semantic rule is `age > 0`; the boundary cases age=0 and age=-1 (which make `age > 0` FALSE) are never generated, so the boundary is not exercised. Similarly the semantic rule `age > 0` is never violated by construction, which is acceptable for a rule but the boundary-coverage target is unmet.
issues.requested_revision: Allow the boundary values -1 and 0 for actor.age to be generated (they are valid INT values and are exactly the comparison-boundary targets), while keeping the dominant distribution within the semantic range. Do not filter out the listed boundary literals.

issues.evidence: spec.ORDER_TIES includes ('musical','Year','ASC') and ('musical','Year','DESC') with tie_at_rank 'any (no LIMIT)', and GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS includes ('musical','Year'). But spec.RANGES ('musical','Year')=(1900,2100) and NumberSampler draws uniformly over that 200-wide range, so with only ~7 generated rows per instance, groups of size >=3 on Year are essentially impossible and order ties on Year are unlikely. _force_group_sizes requires n>=6 and samples 3 distinct values from the pool; with 7 rows it can force a triple, but _force_order_tie then overwrites two positions with the max, potentially destroying the forced group structure. The two Year order-tie entries (ASC and DESC) both call _force_order_tie with the same max-based logic, so only the DESC top is guaranteed; the ASC top (min) is not forced.
issues.requested_revision: Make _force_order_tie respect the direction: for ASC force the minimum value to appear at least twice, for DESC force the maximum. Ensure the Year group-size and order-tie passes do not overwrite each other's planted structure (apply them in a defined order or on disjoint positions).

issues.evidence: The schema declares `FOREIGN KEY ("Musical_ID") REFERENCES "actor"("Actor_ID")` (self-referential, dangling). issues.evidence: Execution summary shows massive row loss: rows_added {musical: 21, actor: 19} vs rows_skipped {musical: 83, actor: 108} across 20 instances. Expected 20*7=140 musical and 20*9=180 actor rows. The writer's row-by-row fallback silently skips rows failing constraints. The spec requires 'rows_skipped stays 0' and 'every instance appends exactly table_sizes_per_instance rows'. The likely cause: PK ranges are relative offsets computed as fresh_pk_start(schema, t, col) - 1 = max(original PK), so [lo+off, hi+off] = [max+1, max+7] for musical — but the compact DB already has 7 musical rows with PKs 1..7, so generated PKs 8..14 should be fine. However, the actual failure is more likely the FK/unique/other constraints or the PK range colliding with compact rows when the compact table already has more than 7 rows. Either way, the writer's silent skip path violates the spec's 'rows_skipped stays 0' requirement and the 'exact table sizes' requirement.
issues.requested_revision: Fix the generation so that every instance appends exactly 7 musical and 9 actor rows with rows_skipped = 0. Diagnose why rows are being skipped (likely PK collisions with compact rows or NOT NULL/unique violations) and correct the PK offset logic and/or the sampler so no row fails. The writer should not silently skip rows; if a row fails, the generation should be corrected upstream, not masked by the fallback.

issues.evidence: Execution summary reports many unmet targets: unmet:group:actor.Musical_ID 15/20, unmet:group:musical.Musical_ID 14/20, unmet:group:musical.Name 19/20, unmet:group:musical.Nominee 19/20, unmet:group:musical.Result 17/20, unmet:group:musical.Year 15/20, unmet:dup:actor.Name 18/20, unmet:dup:actor.Character 14/20, unmet:tie:musical.Year.ASC 5/20, unmet:dup:musical.Nominee 5/20, unmet:tie:musical.Nominee.DESC 4/20, unmet:dup:musical.Result 1/20. issues.evidence: The spec's NULL rule states '5-30% NULL share planted last and never overwritten' for actor.Musical_ID and musical.Nominee. Execution feedback shows actor.Musical_ID: NULL 4/24 and musical.Nominee: NULL 5/21 — these are within 5-30% and have at least one NULL, so the NULL rule is satisfied. issues.evidence: The spec's 'comparison_boundary' for musical.Award lists 12 target values including 'Tony Award', 'tony award', 'Drama Desk Award', 'drama desk award', 'Cleavant Derricks', 'cleavant derricks', ' Aw', ' aw', ' Awa', ' awa', 'Tonyard', 'tonyard'. The EnumSampler draws from enum + boundary + near-variants with probabilities 0.60/0.20/0.10/0.10. The boundary values are drawn at 20% probability, but the spec says near-variants should be at ~10% and the boundary values are the comparison-boundary targets. The spec's 'comparison_boundary' targets are the 12 listed values; the EnumSampler's boundary list is spec.BOUNDARY_VALUES[('musical','Award')] which includes all 12. However, the spec's 'text_enum' rule says 'include near-variants of each literal for comparison-boundary coverage at a small probability (~10%)'. The EnumSampler's 20% boundary draw plus 10% near-variant draw may over-represent boundary values relative to the spec's intent. More importantly, the spec's 'comparison_boundary' targets include 'Cleavant Derricks' and 'cleavant derricks' which are NOT in the enum list ['Tony Award', 'Drama Desk Award'] — these are boundary-only values. The EnumSampler includes them in the pool via boundary, so they can be generated. This is consistent.

However, verify that the 20% boundary draw does not violate the spec's 'small probability (~10%)' for near-variants — the boundary values are distinct from near-variants and the spec lists them as comparison-boundary targets, so 20% is acceptable. No revision needed.

issues.evidence: The spec's 'int_foreign_key' rule says 'Draw from parent primary-key pool with replacement; 5-30% NULL when nullable; plant at least one non-NULL child FK value that matches no parent (unmatched join) and ensure at least one parent row has no children; NULLs are planted last and never overwritten by later passes.' The fill_foreign_keys_consistently function draws from parent values with replacement, but the _plant_nulls function runs AFTER the FK fill and AFTER the group/dup/order passes. The _inject_unmatched_fk runs BEFORE _plant_nulls. So NULLs are planted last — consistent. However, the spec also requires 'ensure at least one parent row has no children'. The code does not explicitly ensure this: with 7 musical rows and 9 actor rows drawing FKs from 7 parent values with replacement, it's possible (though unlikely) that all 7 parents get at least one child. The spec's 'parent_rows_without_children: true' target is not explicitly enforced.
issues.requested_revision: Add explicit enforcement in the generation program (or spec) that at least one parent musical row has no actor children. The current random draw does not guarantee this.
